Can you briefly explain or provide a source to your method of doing so?

If you don't have a super complicated tax situation (i.e. owning your own business, having a lot of dependents, or previous tax issues), then it's actually pretty easy to do. Just estimate what your annual income is going to be, then look up what the standard exemption is for the current tax year, as well as the tax rates. Just do the math and estimate what your tax liability would ultimately be.

Then divide that out between your paychecks and compare what your per-paycheck deduction should be with what it actually is, then either claim fewer allowances on your w-4 (to reduce the amount they take if you're overpaying each week), or add an additional withholding (to increase the amount they take if you're running into large tax liabilities come tax season). Alternatively, you could just claim 99 allowances on your w-4 (then they won't take any taxes out based on the tax tables) and just write in the amount you want them to take each pay period in the additional withholding section.
